title: Check Matrix Rotational Symmetry
description:
Given an `m x n` integer matrix `grid`, determine whether `grid` has **180-degree rotational symmetry** (also known as central point symmetry).

A matrix has 180-degree rotational symmetry if rotating the entire matrix by 180 degrees leaves every cell's value unchanged—equivalently, `grid[r][c] == grid[m - 1 - r][n - 1 - c]` for every `0 <= r < m` and `0 <= c < n`. Return `true` if `grid` is rotationally symmetric, otherwise `false`.
hints: Under a 180-degree rotation, cell (r, c) maps to (m - 1 - r, n - 1 - c).
You only need to check the first half of rows (and the first half of the middle row if m is odd), returning false on the first mismatch.

examples.explanation: Rotating [[1,2,3],[4,5,4],[3,2,1]] by 180 degrees produces the exact same matrix.
Cell (0,0) is 1 while its 180-degree opposite (1,1) is 2, so the matrix is not rotationally symmetric.
Every 1x1 matrix is trivially invariant under a 180-degree rotation.
